blocks.title: Core Concept
blocks.text:
• Biotechnology, essentially deals with industrial scale production of biopharmaceuticals and biologicals using genetically modified microbes, fungi, plants and animals.
  • European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) definition : The integration of natural science and organisms, cells, parts thereof, and molecular analogues for products and services.
• Biotechnology term is given by Karl Ereky.

blocks.title: Previous Year Question 2
blocks.question:
In recombinant DNA technology, the term vectors refers to :-

(1) the enzyme that cuts DNA into restriction fragments

(2) the sticky end of a DNA fragment

(3) a plasmid used to transfer DNA into a living cell

(4) a DNA probe used to identify a particular gene
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

In recombinant DNA technology, the term vector refers to a plasmid or other agent used to transfer DNA into a living cell.
options: (1) the enzyme that cuts DNA into restriction fragments
(2) the sticky end of a DNA fragment
(3) a plasmid used to transfer DNA into a living cell
(4) a DNA probe used to identify a particular gene
blocks.prompt: In recombinant DNA technology, the term vectors refers to :-

blocks.title: Enzymes
blocks.text:
(i) Lysing enzymes :- These enzymes are used for opening the cells to get DNA for genetic experiment.

(ii) Cleaving enzymes (Restriction) :- These enzymes are used to cleave DNA molecules. Cleaving enzymes are of two types;

blocks.title: Restriction Endonuclease Enzymes
blocks.text:
• They are also called molecular scissor or molecular knives due to cutting of DNA molecules.
  • Restriction enzymes belong to a larger class of enzymes called nucleases.
Action of Restriction enzyme :-

  • Sticky end (Free end) :- Restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome sites, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands. e.g. EcoR I, Hind III, BamH I, Sal I
  • Blunt ends (non-sticky end) :- Some enzymes cleave both strands of DNA at exactly the same nucleotide position, typically in the centre of the recognition sequence resulting in blunt end or flush end. e.g. Sma I, EcoR V, Hae III.

blocks.title: Previous Year Questions
blocks.question:
Following statements describe the characteristics of the enzyme Restriction endonuclease. Identify the incorrect statement:

(1) The enzyme cuts DNA molecule at identified position within the DNA

(2) The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands.

(3) The enzyme cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone at specific sites on each strand.

(4) The enzyme recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA.
blocks.answer:
Answer- 2

The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands.

Incorrect- Most restriction endonucleases cut both strands of the DNA at specific sites, producing either blunt or sticky ends.
options: (1) The enzyme cuts DNA molecule at identified position within the DNA
(2) The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands.
(3) The enzyme cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone at specific sites on each strand.
(4) The enzyme recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA.

blocks.title: Previous Year Questions
blocks.question:
The cutting of DNA at specific locations became possible with the discovery of :-

(1) Ligases

(2) Restriction enzymes

(3) Probes

(4) Selectable markers
blocks.answer:
Ans- 2

The cutting of DNA at a specific location became possible with the discovery of restriction enzymes, also known as restriction endonucleases.

These enzymes recognize specific DNA sequences and cut both strands at or near these sites.

This discovery revolutionized molecular biology, making genetic engineering, cloning, and recombinant DNA technology possible.

blocks.question:
Which of the following can act as molecular scissors?

(1) Restriction enzymes

(2) DNA ligase

(3) RNA polymerase

(4) DNA polymerase
blocks.answer:
Ans- 1

Restriction enzymes are a type of endonuclease that cut DNA at or near specific recognition sequences called restriction sites. They make a single incision on each of the two DNA strands.

blocks.title: Previous Year Question
blocks.question:
Given below are two statements one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification

Reason (R) : The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:-

(1) Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

(2) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

(3) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

(4) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
blocks.answer:
Answer - 1

Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification.

  • This statement is correct. PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is a widely used technique to amplify specific DNA sequences.
Reason (R): The ampicillin-resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation.

  • This statement is not relevant to DNA amplification by PCR. It refers to a molecular biology technique where the ampicillin resistance gene is used as a selectable marker in plasmid-based transformation experiments to identify transformed cells, not in PCR.
options: (A) and the other is labelled as Reason
(A) : Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification

blocks.title: Previous Year Questions
blocks.question:
Upon exposure to UV radiation, DNA stained with ethidium bromide will show

(1) Bright blue colour

(2) Bright yellow colour

(3) Bright orange colour

(4) Bright red colour
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

  • Ethidium bromide(EtBr) is a fluorescent dye that intercalates between the bases of DNA.
  • When exposed to ultraviolet (uv) light, EtBr is bound to DNA fluoresces brightly.
  • The fluorescence appears as a bright orange color, making DNA bands visible in techniques like agarose gel electrophoresis.

blocks.title: Previous Year Questions
blocks.question:
Most common matrix is agarose a natural polymer used in gel electrophoresis is extracted from :-

(1) an animal

(2) a fungus

(3) Sea weeds

(4) None of these
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

  • Agarose is a natural polymer that is commonly used as a matrix in gel electrophoresis.
  • It is extracted from red algae ( a type of seaweed), particularly species like Gelidium and Gracilaria.

blocks.title: Previous Year Questions
blocks.question:
In PCR-technology primer is a :-

(1) Small chemically synthesized oligonucleotide that are complementary to region of DNA

(2) Large chemically synthesized oligonucleotide that are identical to region of DNA

(3) Small segment of RNA

(4) None of these
blocks.answer:
Ans- 1

  • In PCR technology, a primer is a short, single-stranded DNA sequence usually 18-25 nucleotides long.
  • It is chemically synthesized in the lab.
  • It is complementary to a specific region on the target DNA strand.
  • Its function is to bind to the template DNA and provide a starting point for DNA polymerase to begin DNA synthesis.
options: (1) Small chemically synthesized oligonucleotide that are complementary to region of DNA
(2) Large chemically synthesized oligonucleotide that are identical to region of DNA

blocks.title: Indirect Method
blocks.text:
(a) Gene Transfer in Bacterial Cell :-

  • In order to force bacteria to take up the plasmid, the bacterial cells must first be made ‘competent’ to take up DNA. This is done by treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation, such as calcium, which increases the efficiency with which DNA enters the bacterium through pores in its cell wall.
  • The bacteria to be used as a host cell should be without plasmids.
  • The host cells are treated with Calcium Chloride.

blocks.title: Previous Year Question
blocks.question:
Which of the following tools of recombinant DNA technology is incorrectly paired with its use?

(1) Restriction enzyme - Production of RFLPs

(2) DNA ligase-that cuts DNA, creating the sticky ends

(3) DNA polymerase - used in a polymerase chain reaction to amplify section of DNA

(4) reverse transcriptase - production of cDNA from mRNA
blocks.answer:
Ans- 2

  • DNA ligase is an enzyme that joins DNA fragments together by forming phosphodiester bonds between the sugar-phosphate backbones.
  • It is not involved in cutting DNA or creating sticky ends.
  • Sticky ends are created by restriction enzymes, not DNA ligase.
options: (2) DNA ligase-that cuts DNA, creating the sticky ends
(3) DNA polymerase - used in a polymerase chain reaction to amplify section of DNA
(4) reverse transcriptase - production of cDNA from mRNA

blocks.title: Previous Year Questions
blocks.question:
Agrobacterium tumefaciens, a pathogen of several dicot plants is able to deliver a piece of DNA and it is known as :-

(1) R-DNA

(2) S-DNA

(3) M-DNA

(4) T-DNA
blocks.answer:
Ans- 4

Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a bacterium that can cause crown gall disease in dicotyledonous plants. It does this by transferring a piece of DNA, called T-DNA, from its tumor-inducing (Ti) plasmid into the plant cell's nucleus. The T-DNA is then integrated into the host genome and transcribed, which causes the plant to develop tumors.

A tumor-inducing plasmid is a large DNA molecule found in the soil bacterium Agrobacterium tumefaciens. It's also found in other species of Agrobacterium, such as A. rubi and A. vitis.

modules.name: Selection of transformant with recombinant DNA

blocks.title: Selection by Two Antibiotic Resistance Gene
blocks.text:
Selection Process:

1. Transformants Selection: Bacteria with the plasmid (transformants) grow on a medium with ampicillin.

2. Recombinants Selection: These transformants are transferred to a medium containing tetracycline.

• Recombinants: Grow on ampicillin but not tetracycline (tetracycline resistance is lost).
    • Non-recombinants: Grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline.

Conclusion:

• One antibiotic resistance gene (ampicillin) selects for transformants.
    • The other antibiotic resistance gene (tetracycline) selects for recombinants.

Insertional Inactivation: This happens when foreign DNA is inserted into a selectable marker gene, causing the gene to lose its function..

blocks.title: Selection by one 𝙇𝙖𝙘 𝙕 gene and one antibiotic resistance gene
blocks.text:
Identifying recombinants by inactivating antibiotic resistance genes is a tedious process since it requires plating on two different antibiotic plates. To simplify this, alternative markers have been developed that use color changes to differentiate recombinants from non-recombinants.

In this method:

• The desired gene is inserted into the coding sequence of an enzyme, typically $\beta-galactosidase$, which results in insertional inactivation.

• A chromogenic substrate, like X-gal, is used:
    • Non-recombinant colonies: Produce $\beta-galactosidase$, turning the colonies blue.

• Recombinant colonies: The enzyme is inactivated, so the colonies remain colorless.

This color-based identification makes it easier to distinguish recombinants.

blocks.title: Previous Year Question
blocks.question:
The two antibiotic resistance genes on vector pBR322 are:-

(1) Ampicillin and Tetracycline

(2) Ampicillin and Chloramphenicol

(3) Chloramphenicol and Tetracycline

(4) Tetracycline and Kanamycin
blocks.answer:
Ans - 1

The two antibiotic resistance genes on the pBR322 plasmid vector are ampicillin (Amp) and tetracycline (Tet):

  • Ampicillin (Amp): The gene bla encodes the ampicillin resistance (AmpR) protein.
  • Tetracycline (Tet): The gene tetA encodes the tetracycline resistance (TetR) protein.

blocks.title: Previous Year Questions
blocks.question:
The restriction enzyme(s) used in recombinant DNA technology making staggered cuts in DNA leaving sticky ends is/are :-

(1) EcoR I

(2) Hind III

(3) BamH I

(4) All of the above
blocks.answer:
Ans- 4

Restriction enzymes are used to cut DNA at recognition sites. The staggered cuts are made in two strands of DNA at different sites, a few nucleotides apart, which produces two strands with protruding ends. These protruding ends are known as sticky ends.
blocks.prompt: The restriction enzyme(s) used in recombinant DNA technology making staggered cuts in DNA leaving sticky ends is/are :-

blocks.title: Previous Year Question
blocks.question:
The sequence that controls the copy number of the linked DNA in the vector, is termed :-

(1) Recognition site

(2) Selectable marker

(3) Ori site

(4) Palindromic sequence
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

The sequence that controls the copy number of linked DNA in a vector is called the ori site, which stands for "Origin of Replication". The ori site is where DNA replication begins, and it allows plasmids to replicate themselves inside cells. Plasmids use the host's machinery to create extra copies.

blocks.title: Core Concept
blocks.text:
• If any protein - encoding gene is expressed in a heterologous host, it is called a recombinant protein.
  • Recombinant host cell is cultured in large tanks called bioreactors in optimum conditions (temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, oxygen)

blocks.title: Bioreactors
blocks.text:
• The most commonly used bioreactors are of stirred type.
  • A stirred - tank reactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reactor contents.
  • The stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor. Alternatively, air can be bubbled through the reactor.
  • The bioreactor has an agitator system, an oxygen delivery system and a foam control system, a temperature control system, pH control system and sampling ports so that small volumes of the culture can be withdrawn periodically.

blocks.title: Downstream Processing
blocks.text:
• It refers to the separation and purification processes of fermentation/enzyme reaction into desired products.
  • Accounts for 60% of the total production costs.

blocks.title: Previous Year Question
blocks.question:
The most commonly used bioreactors are of:-

(1) Simple stirring type

(2) Sparged stirring type

(3) Both (1) and (2)

(4) None of the above
blocks.answer:
Ans. 3

The most commonly used bioreactors are simple and sparged stirred tank bioreactors.
